prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Sugar Land, Texas, and has concussion. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1429; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my name on a recording right now, but you already have it on the claim file.

Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the accident happened?

A: I was driving on a main road in Sugar Land, heading toward the shopping center. Traffic had slowed down in front of me, so I was already stopped at a light.

Q: What happened next?

A: The car behind me didn't stop in time. I felt a hard jolt from behind, and my head snapped forward and then back against the headrest.

Q: Did you lose consciousness or hit your head on anything?

A: I don't think I lost consciousness, but I hit my head on the side window. I remember feeling dizzy and my ears were ringing.

Q: Did you get out of the vehicle or seek medical attention at the scene?

A: I stayed in the car for a few minutes until the police arrived. An ambulance came and they checked me over, but I told them I felt okay at the time.

Q: How are you feeling now?

A: Not great. I have headaches almost every day, and bright lights bother my eyes. I get tired by the afternoon and I've had trouble concentrating at work.

Q: Have you seen a doctor since the accident?

A: Yes, I've been to my primary care doctor twice and I've started seeing a neurologist. They said it's a concussion and told me to limit screen time and rest as much as I can.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add about the accident?

A: Only that I was stopped and not at fault. I just want to get my car repaired and get back to normal.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
